items.title: Three-dimensional radial Carleman inequality with integer weight
items.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $s\ge1$ be an integer and put $\tau=s+1$. Write $r(x)=|x|$ for $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and let $\Delta$ be the Euclidean Laplacian ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Then for every $u\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$,
$$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}\le\frac{2}{s}\,\|r^{-\tau+2}\Delta u\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^3)}.$$
Moreover, if $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ is compactly supported in an annulus $\{0<a\le|x|\le b\}$, then the weak second derivatives of $u$ exist as locally square integrable functions, $\Delta u$ denotes their sum in the weak sense ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), and the same inequality holds for $u$. The weight $r^{-\tau+2}$ is bounded on every fixed compact annulus but is not integrable at the origin, and this is exactly why the density extension is stated for functions whose support stays away from $r=0$. The constant $2/s$ is explicit and is not claimed to be sharp.
items.strategy:
Change of variables. Write $x=rn$ with $r=e^{-t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, $n\in S^2$, and set $u(rn)=r^{-1/2}v(t,n)$, $w(t,n)=e^{st}v(t,n)$. The polar-coordinates formula ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]) and the one-dimensional substitution ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) give $dx=r^3\,dt\,d\sigma(n)$, and with $u^2=r^{-1}v^2$ and $\tau-1=s$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau}u^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}w^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
The radial computation ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) $\Delta u=r^{-5/2}(\partial_t^2v+\Delta_{S^2}v-\tfrac14v)$ and the substitution $v=e^{-st}w$ give $\partial_t^2v=e^{-st}(\partial_t-s)^2w$; the same factor $e^{2st}$ occurs in $r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2r^3\,dt\,d\sigma$, hence
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}r^{-2\tau+4}(\Delta u)^2\,dx=\int_{\mathbb R}\int_{S^2}\bigl|\bigl((\partial_t-s)^2+\Delta_{S^2}-\tfrac14\bigr)w\bigr|^2\,d\sigma\,dt.$$
Modal decomposition. Expand $w(t,\cdot)$ for almost every $t$ in the complete orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics ([[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]]) and use the eigenvalue identity $\Delta_{S^2}Y_{lm}=-l(l+1)Y_{lm}$, a direct computation from the homogeneous extension: $H_l$ is a homogeneous harmonic polynomial and $\Delta=\partial_r^2+2r^{-1}\partial_r+r^{-2}\Delta_{S^2}$ gives $0=r^{-2}(l^2+l+\Delta_{S^2})H_l$. Parseval ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]) and monotone convergence identify the two displayed integrals with the sums of the modal norms $\sum_{l,m}\|w_{lm}\|^2$ and $\sum_{l,m}\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|^2$. Fourier multiplier. In the $2\pi$ convention of [[thm-fourier-differentiation-and-multiplication-identities-on-tempered-distributions]] and Plancherel ([[thm-plancherel]]) the mode operator has symbol $(2\pi i\xi-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2$; with $x=4\pi^2\xi^2\ge0$, $A=s-l-\tfrac12$ and $B=s+l+\tfrac12$, its squared modulus is $(x+A^2)(x+B^2)$, which is increasing in $x\ge0$ and therefore at least $A^2B^2=(s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)^2$. For integers $l\ge0$ and $s\ge1$ the integer $l$ minimizing $|s^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2|$ is $l=s-1$ or $l=s$, with value $s-\tfrac14\ge\tfrac s2$, so the squared modulus is at least $s^2/4$. Hence $\|w_{lm}\|\le\tfrac2s\|((\partial_t-s)^2-(l+\tfrac12)^2)w_{lm}\|$ for every mode, and summing the nonnegative squared modal norms gives the inequality for smooth compactly supported $u$. Density extension. On a fixed annulus $a\le r\le b$ the weights $r^{\pm\tau}$, $r^{-\tau+2}$ are bounded. Approximate $u\in H^2(\mathbb R^3)$ with support in that annulus in the $H^2$ norm by $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ functions ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]]), multiply each approximant by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighbourhood of the support of $u$ and vanishing near the origin ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]); the products lie in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$, still converge to $u$ in $H^2$, and because the weights are bounded on the fixed annulus both sides of the inequality pass to the limit. Countable Choice is declared because it is assumed by [[thm-plancherel]] and by the density corollary; no other choice principle is used.

references.title: D. Tataru, Carleman estimates, unique continuation and applications (Northwestern University, 1998 monograph draft), Chapter 3.6: Theorem 3.50 with Corollary 3.6.1 (singular-weight estimates for the Laplacian) and Theorem 3.52 (strong unique continuation)
S. Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155: Plancherel (Definition 11.22, Theorem 11.29) and the Fourier differentiation identities (Section 12.1)

items.title: Weak unique continuation for bounded potentials in three dimensions
items.design_state: local-research-proof-written; exact-hypotheses-retained; not published and not engine-certified
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be nonempty, open and connected, let $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let $\psi\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ satisfy $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ in the distributional sense: $\int_\Omega\psi\,\Delta\varphi\,dx=\int_\Omega V\psi\,\varphi\,dx$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, with $\Delta\varphi$ the classical Laplacian. Here $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ denotes the locally integrable classes on $\Omega$ whose weak derivatives of every order at most two exist and are locally square integrable ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); $V\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ means $V$ is measurable and $\|V\|_\infty<\infty$ on every compact subset ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]], [[def-l-infinity-on-a-measure-space]]). If $\psi=0$ on a nonempty open subset of $\Omega$, then $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. No smoothness, sign, symmetry or decay hypothesis on $V$ beyond local essential boundedness is used, and no analyticity is assumed.
items.strategy:
Local propagation step. Let $z\in\Omega$ be a point on a neighbourhood of which $\psi=0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline B_R(z)\subseteq\Omega$; translate the origin to $z$ so that the weight of the Carleman lemma is measured from $z$. Choose $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(0);[0,1])$ with $\chi=1$ on $B_{R/2}(0)$ ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]) and put $u=\chi\psi$. By the smooth-factor Leibniz rule with $|\alpha|\le2$ ([[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]]) $u$ has weak derivatives up to order two in $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$, is compactly supported in $B_R(0)$ and vanishes near $0$; since $\Delta\psi=V\psi$ distributionally, $\Delta u=Vu+e$ with $e=2\nabla\chi\cdot\nabla\psi+(\Delta\chi)\psi$, supported in the annulus $\{R/2\le|x|\le R\}$. Apply the radial Carleman lemma with parameter $s\ge4MR^2$, where $M=\|V\|_\infty$ on $B_R$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]): using $r\le R$ on the ball and $|V|\le M$, $\|r^{-\tau}Vu\|\le MR^2\|r^{-\tau}u\|$, and the lemma plus absorption of the term $\tfrac12\|r^{-\tau}u\|$ gives
$$\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac4s\|r^{-\tau+2}e\|_2.$$
For $0<\rho<R/2$ one has $u=\psi$ on $B_\rho(0)$ and $r^{-\tau}\ge\rho^{-\tau}$ there, while $e$ is supported where $r\le R$, so
$$\|\psi\|_{L^2(B_\rho(0))}\le\rho^{\tau}\|r^{-\tau}u\|_2\le\frac{4R^2}{s}\Bigl(\frac{2\rho}{R}\Bigr)^{\tau}\|e\|_2\longrightarrow0\qquad(s\to\infty),$$
as $e$ is fixed. Hence $\psi=0$ on $B_{R/2}(z)$: vanishing near a point propagates to the ball of half the radius of any ball around that point that is relatively compact in $\Omega$. Global propagation. Let $Z$ be the union of the open sets on which $\psi$ vanishes; $Z$ is open and nonempty by hypothesis. Fix $x\in\Omega$ and a polygonal path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\Omega$ from a point of $Z$ to $x$, which exists because $\Omega$ is a connected open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-connected-space]], [[cor-components-of-open-subsets-of-rn-are-polygonally-connected]], [[def-polygonal-path-and-polygonal-connectedness]]). The image $\gamma([0,1])$ is compact and disjoint from the closed set $\mathbb R^3\setminus\Omega$, so it has distance $\delta>0$ from it ([[lem-relative-compact-closed-sets-have-a-positive-distance-gap]]). By uniform continuity of $\gamma$ on $[0,1]$ choose $0=t_0<\dots<t_N=1$ with $|\gamma(t_{j+1})-\gamma(t_j)|<\delta/4$. Inductively, if $\psi=0$ near $\gamma(t_j)$, then $B_{\delta/2}(\gamma(t_j))$ has closure in $\Omega$, so the propagation step with $R=\delta/2$ gives $\psi=0$ on $B_{\delta/4}(\gamma(t_j))$, a neighbourhood of $\gamma(t_{j+1})$; hence $\psi=0$ near $x=\gamma(t_N)$. As $x\in\Omega$ was arbitrary, $Z=\Omega$. Consequently $\Omega\setminus Z$, which is open in $\Omega$, is empty: otherwise $Z,\Omega\setminus Z$ would be a separation of $\Omega$ ([[def-connected-space]]). This proves $\psi=0$ on $\Omega$. Countable Choice is inherited through the Carleman lemma; no further choice principle is used.

references.title: B. Davey, Quantitative unique continuation for the Laplacian plus a potential (arXiv:1903.04021)
D. Tataru, Carleman estimates, unique continuation and applications (Northwestern University monograph, 1998)

items.title: Exterior spherical multipole expansion and the ball boundary series
items.statement:
Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ vanish outside $\overline B_a(0)$. Use the complete orthonormal basis $\{Y_{lm}\}$ of real spherical harmonics on $S^2$ with unnormalised surface measure $d\sigma$ of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], and the Legendre generating kernel and its compact remainder bound from [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]. Write $x=rn$, $r=|x|$, $n\in S^2$. Then:
(a) **Exterior multipole expansion.** For every $x$ with $|x|>a$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)\rho(y)\,dy,$$
the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with tail after degree $N$ bounded by $\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}/(r_0^{N+2}(1-a/r_0))$; the degree-$l$ term is the $L^2(S^2)$ projection of $y\mapsto|x-y|^{-1}\rho(y)$ onto the degree-$l$ harmonics. The degree-zero and degree-one terms are the Coulomb and dipole terms with the explicit remainder bound of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] ($Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)\,dy$, $|R(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$).
(b) **Termwise differentiation.** On every compact $K$ with $\inf_K|x|>a$ the series may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on $K$; in particular the potential is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$.
(c) **Ball boundary branch.** For $f\in L^2(S^2)$ with coefficients $f_{lm}$ the series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ converges in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$ and, with all derivatives, uniformly on each closed ball of radius $<1$, is harmonic on the open unit ball, and is the unique harmonic function there with a finite $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\cdot)\|_2$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$; for continuous $f$ it equals the Poisson integral $(1-r^2)/(4\pi|rn-n'|^3)$ of $f$ and extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary values $f$. This is a statement about the Newtonian integral of a compactly supported $L^1$ density and about harmonic functions; no physical charge distribution or electrostatic interpretation is asserted.
items.strategy: Assembly of the recorded branches. Write $q=|y|/r$ and $z=n\cdot y/|y|$ for $y\ne0$; the convergent Legendre kernel [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]] gives $|x-y|^{-1}=\sum_l(|y|^l/r^{l+1})P_l(z)$ for $|y|\le a<r$, with the stated geometric tail, and integration against the finite measure $\rho\,dy$ yields the zonal multipole series with the displayed error times $\|\rho\|_1$. Substituting the addition theorem $P_l(z)=\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\sum_mY_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(y/|y|)$ from [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] into the $l$-th term and separating variables gives the displayed spherical-harmonic coefficients, the finite sums agreeing with the zonal series for every degree, hence in the uniform limit. The degree-zero and degree-one coefficients are $Q$ and the components of $p$, and comparison with the explicit Coulomb-dipole splitting of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] (twice the fundamental theorem applied to $h(s)=|x-sy|^{-1}$) identifies the remainder and its bound. For (b), differentiate the zonal kernel with respect to the observation variable on a compact set disjoint from $\overline B_a$: the analytic integrand admits a complex parameter disk bounded away from its zeros, so Cauchy estimates bound each fixed spatial derivative of the $l$-th term by a polynomial in $l$ times $(a/r_0)^l$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]); the ratio test gives uniform convergence of the differentiated series, and the harmonic/integral representations identify the limit with the corresponding derivative, using the inner product conventions of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and the differentiability framework of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. For (c), the addition theorem gives $\sum_m|Y_{lm}(n)|^2=(2l+1)/4\pi$, so Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the absolute tail at fixed $r<1$ by $\|f\|_2(\sum_{l>N}r^{2l}(2l+1)/4\pi)^{1/2}\to0$; the derivative estimates and the interior harmonic estimates of [[lem-em-ball-poisson-series-boundary-convergence]] give uniform convergence of all derivatives on smaller balls, orthogonality gives $\|u(r\cdot)-f\|_2\to0$, and the radial ODE argument quoted there (two solutions $r^l$, $r^{-l-1}$, smoothness at the centre excluding the second) gives uniqueness in the stated class; the Poisson kernel identity and uniform boundary convergence for continuous $f$ are the last part of that lemma. Completeness and orthonormality of the basis are those of [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]].

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis)

S. Axler, P. Bourdon, W. Ramey, Harmonic Function Theory, 2nd ed. (Springer GTM 137), author-hosted full text, Chapter 5 (harmonic polynomials, spherical harmonics and zonal harmonics) and Chapter 1 (Poisson kernel for the ball)

items.title: Well-posed weak solvability and classical regularity for declared smooth-domain elliptic boundary problems
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability lemmas. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] is the local graph definition used throughout), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive ($\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ on $\Omega$ for some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$), and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. Then:
(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ pointwise with $u|_{\partial\Omega}=g$.
(b) **Neumann.** For every smooth outward conormal datum $g$ satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$, there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$. It is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ for each component gives a unique normalised solution, smooth on each closed component. In particular on a connected domain the compatibility is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$, with a single additive constant.
(c) **Transmission.** For the stated finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth uniformly positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth bulk $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b). The weak right-hand side includes $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$ and, in the Neumann case, $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique. With outer Neumann data it exists exactly when the total right-hand side vanishes on the constant of each connected component, equivalently $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for each $j$, and is unique modulo componentwise constants; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. In either case the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]].
Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this item states the combined existence-and-regularity theorem on the declared domains.
items.strategy: The claim collects three recorded branches and their compatibility. (a) Existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence are [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the classical upgrade to $C^\infty$ on the closure, with the classical equation and boundary values, is [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (b) Testing the displayed weak identity with the constant on each component gives $\int_{\Omega_j}\rho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$, including the minus sign when solved for the outer conormal integral. Necessity of componentwise compatibility, existence, uniqueness modulo componentwise constants and the normalised form are [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; the classical upgrade is again [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]]. (c) Apply the transmission functional including the sheet-charge term, with outer Dirichlet tests in $H_0^1$ for full uniqueness, or outer Neumann tests in $H^1$ with that functional zero on every componentwise constant and the chosen mean normalisation. The weak existence and the one-sided trace identity are the transmission part of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], the two-sided classical smoothness and the jump relation are [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], and the passage from the weak identity to the interface flux uses the divergence theorem for the piecewise smooth configuration together with the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]. The smooth coefficients, conormal field and chart changes are smooth by the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]; the inner products and the quadratic form $\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u$ use the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No existence or regularity claim is made beyond the stated smooth-domain, finite-interface regime.

items.title: Uniqueness of the outgoing scalar Helmholtz solution with a smooth obstacle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the modal DtN/trace suppliers, covering the Countable Choice used by the local UCP supplier. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]) whose exterior $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ is connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. Suppose $u$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ on $D$ with the Euclidean Laplacian $\Delta$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), vanishes on $\partial O$, and is outgoing in the class of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: its trace $f=u|_{S_R}$ lies in $H^{1/2}(S_R)$ and its normal derivative on $S_R$ is $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense of that lemma. Then $u=0$ on $D$. No decay rate, asymptotic expansion or pointwise Sommerfeld formula beyond the stated outgoing class is assumed.
items.strategy: Green's identity on the truncated exterior. Apply the first Green identity [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] to $u$ and its complex conjugate on the bounded $C^1$ domain $D\cap B_R$, whose boundary consists of $\partial O$ and $S_R$: the volume integral is the real number $\int_{D\cap B_R}(|\nabla u|^2-k^2|u|^2)\,dx$, and the inner boundary contributes zero because $u=0$ on $\partial O$. The full boundary pairing equals that real volume integral, so its imaginary part is zero; its real part need not vanish. Thus $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=0$. By [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] applied to $f$ the imaginary part is $\operatorname{Im}\langle T_Rf,f\rangle=\sum_{l,m}(\operatorname{Im}t_l)|f_{lm}|^2$ with $\operatorname{Im}t_l>0$ for every $l$; the already established zero imaginary pairing and the strictly positive modal coefficients force every $f_{lm}=0$. Consequently the outgoing exterior series of that lemma, which is the unique outgoing finite-local-energy solution with trace $f$ on $S_R$, vanishes on $\{r>R\}$; combined with $u=0$ on $\partial O$ the function $u$ vanishes on the complement of $D\cap\overline B_R$. Propagation. On $D$ the real and imaginary parts of $u$ are $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solutions of $\Delta w=Vw$ with the bounded coefficient $V=-k^2$, so [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] applies to each of them on the connected open $D$: each vanishes on the nonempty open set $D\cap\{r>R\}$, hence on $D$. Therefore $u=0$ on $D$. No finite experimental observation or physical postulate is used.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness for the smooth exterior vector Helmholtz mixed boundary problem
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers (and, for the exterior branch, the Fredholm alternative). Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, let $D=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ be connected, let $k>0$, and let $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$. For every smooth tangent field $e_T$ on $\partial O$ there is exactly one field $E$, $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, satisfying, with the Euclidean Laplacian acting componentwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]),
$$(\Delta+k^2)E=0\ \text{ on }D,\qquad \operatorname{div}E=0\ \text{ on }D,\qquad E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T\ \text{ on }\partial O,$$
and outgoing on the large sphere $S_R$ in the modal sense of [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]. Given the prescribed tangential trace and $\operatorname{div}E=0$, the corresponding normal closure is the relation $\partial_nE_n+(\operatorname{div}n)E_n=-\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T$ with $n$ the outward normal of the truncated exterior region $B_R\setminus\overline O$ (pointing into $O$ on the inner boundary). This is the explicit Maxwell boundary closure used by the PEC scattering consumer; three independent scalar Dirichlet data are not asserted to be equivalent.
items.strategy:
Reduction to a coercive shifted form. On the truncated annulus $A=B_R\setminus\overline O$ introduce $X=\{v\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3):v_{	ext{tangential}}=0	ext{ on }\partial O\}$, a closed subspace of $H^1$ by the trace continuity of [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]; the trace machinery is smooth for the classical solutions. With $\kappa=\operatorname{div}n$ on the inner boundary, the form
$$a(E,v)=\int_A igl(
abla E:\overline{
abla v}-k^2E\cdot\overline v igr)+\int_{\partial O}\kappa E_n\overline{v_n}-\langle T_RE,vangle_{S_R}$$
is bounded on $H^1$ by [[lem-em-sphere-outgoing-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]] and bounded $\kappa$. Its real part is coercive after shifting by a real $\lambda>k^2+C_\delta+1$: the outer term is nonnegative by the sign of $\operatorname{Re}T_R$, and the curvature term is absorbed by the collar inequality proved in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] with $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$. The complex coercive form is inverted by the explicit contraction iteration (Hilbert Riesz representation [[thm-riesz-representation-for-hilbert-space]] turns the shifted form into a bounded operator $B$ with $\operatorname{Re}\langle Bx,xangle\ge\alpha\|x\|^2$; for small $t>0$, $x\mapsto(I-tB)x+tf$ is a strict contraction in the complete space). The $L^2$ pairing $J:X	o X^*$ is compact because the argument of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] gives $X\hookrightarrow L^2$ compact on the smooth bounded domain $A$; the original form operator is a shifted inverse composed with $I-\lambda K$, $K$ compact, so the Fredholm alternative [[thm-fredholm-alternative-for-identity-minus-compact]] (with its Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) gives bounded invertibility once the kernel is zero. Kernel. For a homogeneous solution the imaginary part of $a(E,E)$ is $-\operatorname{Im}\langle T_RE,Eangle=0$, and the strictly positive DtN imaginary coefficients force all three outer traces of $E$ to vanish. Extending the field by the outgoing series outside $B_R$ and integrating by parts with [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] gives a weak componentwise Helmholtz solution on $D$ with $H^1$ regularity on each bounded local patch, because the full traces agree across $S_R$, and it vanishes outside $B_R$. On each such patch apply [[thm-interior-h-two-regularity-for-divergence-form-equations]] with principal matrix $I$, $b=0$, $c=-k^2$, $f=0$ (equivalently $-\Delta E=k^2E$), giving $H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$. The real and imaginary parts of each component then satisfy $\Delta w=-k^2w$ on the connected $D$ and vanish on its nonempty exterior open subset, so the direct local supplier [[thm-bounded-potential-weak-unique-continuation-in-three-dimensions]] makes them zero. No scalar inner Dirichlet condition is inferred from tangential PEC data, and the scalar exterior-Dirichlet lemma is not invoked in this kernel step. Hence the kernel is zero and the shifted-then-unshifted problem is boundedly invertible. Inhomogeneous data. For prescribed smooth $e_T$, give each Cartesian scalar component the Dirichlet boundary datum $(e_T)_j$ on $\partial O$ and zero on $S_R$. The weak prescribed-trace solver [[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]] with principal coefficient $I$ and zero bulk source, followed by the scalar smooth-data upgrade [[lem-em-smooth-domain-elliptic-regularity]], supplies a smooth componentwise lift $G$ on $\overline A$ with $G|_{\partial O}=e_T$ and $G|_{S_R}=0$ (apply to real and imaginary parts). This is a genuine scalar use of B7, distinct from the inline vector mixed-boundary regularity proof. Now solve for $u\in X$ with $a(u,v)=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}$; $E=G+u$ then has the prescribed tangential trace, and testing against compactly supported interior fields gives the componentwise Helmholtz equation and the stated normal relation. Regularity. At the artificial sphere the matched traces and normal derivatives make the extended field a weak Helmholtz solution across $S_R$, so [[cor-smooth-data-give-smooth-interior-solutions]] applied on bounded local patches to the constant-coefficient operator $-\Delta-k^2$ makes the matched field smooth there; no boundary theorem is used at this artificial interior surface. At $\partial O$ rotate into a smooth frame with two tangential components and one normal component; the principal part becomes a uniformly elliptic scalar principal matrix times the identity with smooth lower-order coupling, and the boundary system (two Dirichlet components and one Robin component) is complementing: in the frozen half-space a decaying principal mode $e^{i\xi\cdot y-|\xi|t}a$ with $\xi
e0$ has $a_1=a_2=0$ and $-|\xi|a_3=0$, so all amplitudes vanish, while curvature and connection terms are lower order. Supply the vector boundary argument inline, rather than treating B7's scalar public statement as a vector theorem. After the smooth frame rotation and boundary flattening, tangential shifts preserve the two zero Dirichlet component traces, while the normal component has arbitrary admissible trace. Test with $-\delta_{-h}(\eta^2\delta_h u)$ componentwise. The scalar principal matrix times the identity gives the sum of three positive gradient squares; smooth coefficient and frame commutators are lower-order $L^2$ terms bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz and Young. The differenced Robin boundary term consists of the bounded Robin coefficient times the normal quotient trace square and its smooth coefficient commutator; the collar estimate $\|w\|_{L^2(\partial O)}^2\le\delta\|
abla w\|_2^2+C_\delta\|w\|_2^2$ absorbs the first term, and trace continuity and Young bound the commutator by the same gradient bound and known $H^1$ data. This gives uniform tangential quotient-gradient bounds. Riesz identifies all mixed second derivatives in $L^2$, and the corrected component equation recovers each normal second derivative using the uniformly positive normal principal coefficient. Iterate the tangential quotient argument with differentiated smooth data and coefficient/Robin commutators, and recover remaining normal orders from the component equations; a finite boundary cover gives all orders. Local Sobolev extension/embedding then gives classical smooth representatives. This is the actual inline mixed-boundary product-space proof obligation, with two Dirichlet components and one Robin component; it is not replaced by a scalar Dirichlet-regularity citation. Divergence. The scalar $q=\operatorname{div}E$ is a smooth Helmholtz solution on $D$; the divergence identity in a boundary frame turns the inner Robin relation into $q=0$ on $\partial O$, and the outgoing component series differentiates to an outgoing $q$; [[lem-em-exterior-outgoing-scalar-uniqueness]] then gives $q=0$ on $D$. Thus $\operatorname{div}E=0$ is deduced, not presumed.

items.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. The associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ has coefficients $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, converges in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data, and retains the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The classical smoothness of the eigenfields on the declared smooth domain, and the solvability of the shifted auxiliary boundary problems used in the construction, are those supplied by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] on $\Omega$.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For a rectangular box the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
items.strategy: The smooth-cavity assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], whose proof constructs the compact self-adjoint solution operator of the shifted problem with the coercive solver and the smooth-domain interior estimate, applies the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem to obtain the eigenbasis and the multiplicities, and derives the distributional eigen-equation and the modal wave expansion with zero modes retained. This item records the composition with the elliptic existence theorem of this page: [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] supplies the weak solvability and the classical ($C^\infty$-on-the-closure) upgrade on the bounded smooth domain for the elliptic boundary problems used in the closure argument, so the eigenfields and the auxiliary problems live on the declared smooth class; the quadratic graph forms and the curl/div expressions are computed with the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. The rectangular assertions are the recorded $G2$ content of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]]: the reflection parities convert the boundary class into a rectangular torus class, the imported one-dimensional complete trigonometric system and Hilbert Fourier expansion give product completeness, and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE with conservation of $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$ gives the unique weak solution and energy conservation; the direct TE/TM mode verification is the recorded physics branch G1 on the guide page and is not a mathematical dependency here. The recorded K10 branch (uniform Ohmic loss) is a physical-model branch of the same modal argument and is homed on the physical page, not here.

title: Em Boundary And Spectral Prerequisites — Examples

items.title: Explicit mathematical hypothesis/convention examples
items.statement: Three exact boundary checks. (i) The sphere trace $f(n)=n_3$ is the trace of the homogeneous degree-one harmonic polynomial $u(x)=x_3$, so the ball boundary branch of [[thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis]] applies to it; the simultaneous conditions $\Delta u=0$ in the unit ball $B_1$ and $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$ are incompatible, because the divergence theorem gives $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,dx=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma=\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$. (ii) For the coefficient $\varepsilon=1$ on $\{x_1<0\}$ and $\varepsilon=2$ on $\{x_1>0\}$, the function $u=x_1$ on the first side and $u=x_1/2$ on the second is continuous and locally $H^1$, and $\varepsilon\partial_1u\equiv1$, so $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=0$ weakly although $u$ is not $C^1$: its first derivative jumps from $1$ to $1/2$ across the interface. Hence the smooth-coefficient statements of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] cannot be extended to this piecewise-constant case, and the correct conclusion there is the piecewise regularity recorded by that item, not a global $C^1$ or $C^\infty$-on-the-closure statement. (iii) The same wild-coefficient configuration is a hypothesis boundary for the smooth-domain spectral completeness of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]: its coefficients and interfaces are exactly the ones excluded from the smooth $C^\infty$ PEC/smooth-domain hypotheses, and the explicit solution shows that a global classical conclusion fails while the weak $H^1$ formulation remains valid. All three parts are exact finite computations or classical divergence-theorem evaluations; they assert no physical interpretation.
items.strategy:
Direct computations. Part (i): $\Delta x_3=0$ and $
abla x_3=e_3$, so on the unit sphere $\partial_nx_3=e_3\cdot n=n_3$; if a function were harmonic in $B_1$ with $\partial_nu=1$ on $S^2$, the divergence theorem [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to $
abla u$ (a $C^1$ field) would give $0=\int_{B_1}\Delta u\,d\lambda=\int_{S^2}\partial_nu\,d\sigma$, while the polar-coordinates formula [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] and the defining normalisation give $\sigma(S^2)=3\lambda_3(B_1)=4\pi$; the contradiction $0=4\pi$ proves incompatibility, and the Laplacian is that of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. Part (ii): on each open half-space the field $\varepsilon
abla u$ is the constant $(1,0,0)$, so its distributional divergence is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]): testing $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)$ against a compactly supported smooth test function and integrating by parts reduces to $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\partial_1\varphi\cdot(-1)\,dx=0$ for a constant field. The function $u$ is continuous because $x_1$ and $x_1/2$ both tend to $0$ at the interface, its distributional first derivatives are the locally integrable functions equal to $1,0,0$ respectively $1/2,0,0$ on the two sides ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), and these representatives jump at $x_1=0$, so $u$ is $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but not $C^1$. Part (iii): this is the statement that the excluded case is excluded: the smooth coefficients and smooth interfaces required by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] and by the smooth-domain class of [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]] fail, while the displayed weak solution exists and is not smooth on the closure. No physical postulate, measurement or empirical claim is used.
